events.excerpt: CSR SpMM does substantial work per sparse row when each row has many nonzeros and the dense RHS has a large column dimension. Account for that work when choosing the row parallel grain size so rows are split more aggressively for these cases. Also inline the per-nonzero dense-row accumulation instead of calling cpublas::axpy<scalar_t>(...) for each nonzero. This explicit template call dispatches through axpy_stub to a generic strided loop, rather than calling a BLAS overload. Inlining removes one dispatch-stub call per nonzero while retaining support for non-contiguous dense and result tensors, with a separate contiguous inner loop that is straightforward for the compiler to optimize. Add a correctness test for non-contiguous dense RHS and output tensors, covering floating-point and complex dtypes. Pull Request resolved: #188237 Approved by: https://github.com/amjames , https://github.com/pearu
events.headline: viable/strict/1794585028: Optimize CSR SpMM CPU grain size and inner accumulation (#188237)

events.excerpt: Researchers from Hanbat National University and the Samsung Advanced Institute of Technology have come up with a way to boost the efficiency and lifespan of organic light-emitting diode (OLED) displays — with the addition of a thin additional layer designed to prevent the formation of "holes" created by excess positive charges. "Organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) are typically affected by nonradiative energy loss originating from interfacial charge accumulation and exciton quenching processes," the researchers explain of their focus in the project. "In particular, spontaneous orientation polarization in organic thin films generates a giant surface potential (GSP), which modifies the interfacial electrostatic environment and induces unintended charge injection and charge accumulation near the emitting layer (EML). These excess charge carriers increase the polaron density in the EML and promote exciton–polaron quenching, which limits device efficiency and stability." To simplify: the efficiency of current OLED display panels is limited owing to an internal molecular alignment causing the gathering of excess positive charges, effective "holes," near the light-emitting layer which then reduce its ability to produce light efficiently. events.excerpt: I’d like feedback on a draft ERC that says how a wallet derives hash-based post-quantum keys (leanSPHINCS, SLH-DSA, WOTS, FORS, XMSS) from a BIP-39 phrase. Draft: Add ERC: Hash-Based Key Derivation from BIP-39 by johba37 · Pull Request #2172 · ethereum/ERCs · GitHub Why Contracts already verify hash-based signatures through ERC-1271 and account abstraction, and EIP-8288 would aggregate leanSPHINCS. Users back their accounts up with BIP-39 phrases, but no standard says how a phrase becomes a hash-based key, and implementations have diverged: from the BIP-39 entropy, with Keccak-256 over application labels (the Winterlock signer I work on does this today); through a second PBKDF2 over the phrase with its own salt ( WOTS-39 ); through HMAC-SHA512 over the BIP-39 seed under its own label (a hardware wallet in development). So the same phrase gives different keys in different wallets, and restoring it elsewhere does not restore the keys. A wallet that already has BIP-32 might derive these keys through it. That would bring a problem of its own. Every BIP-32 node has an elliptic-curve public key. And yet there they all were, a mere five weeks before the midterm elections, gathered at the White House to smile for photos with President Trump and sign on to his “Super Intelligence” agenda. Even by the diminished standards of today’s corporate governance, this was a shockingly foolish decision. Despite dozens of polls showing a rising tide of anti-Trump sentiment and bipartisan rejection of AI and data centers , the futurists of the tech elite cast aside long-term corporate interests for short-term political favor. And now, their industry is very squarely in the new victors’ crosshairs . He’s been working on a set of guidelines for researchers developing brain-computer interfaces (BCIs). Ethics guidelines for clinical trials already exist. But BCI trials are different, says Jennifer Chandler, a professor of law and neuroethics at the University of Ottawa who also worked on the guidelines. “These are people who have a device embedded in their brain, are in trials sometimes for years and years … [and contribute] a significant investment of time, of the body, and of intellectual effort.” Burkhart was left paralyzed from the chest down following a diving accident in 2010, when he was 19 years old. Around four years later, he volunteered to become the first person to trial a brain implant designed for hand control. events.excerpt: Only a handful of NHS trusts are using the cancer app on the controversial £330 million Federated Data Platform (FDP) run by Palantir, while newly released figures raise questions about which trusts are benefiting. Cancer 360 was designed to bring cancer patients' data from disparate spreadsheets and electronic health records into a central system, helping health professionals prioritize treatment. Pilots began four years ago, and trusts are not charged directly for the FDP. Yet official figures put Cancer 360's uptake at just five or six trusts. Freedom of Information responses gathered by grassroots campaign group No Palantir in the NHS also reveal discrepancies between reported benefits and recorded use. In June 2025, NHS England said that Cancer 360 "drastically cut down diagnosis times" and referred to a pilot at Chelsea and Westminster NHS Foundation Trust, which saw the proportion of patients diagnosed within 28 days climb from 72 percent to 85 percent. events.excerpt: Nixie clocks have become popular enough that these days there’s no shortage of turn-key options that let you experience that warm glow with a minimum of fuss. Many still come as little more than a bare PCB, giving the purchaser some freedom to come up with their own enclosure, but at least the electronics are handled. But for [Justin Scott], putting his new two-digit Nixie clock board into a handsome box was only half the battle . He also wanted to do something a bit more interesting than just tell the time. To convert the board from a simple clock to a device that could show how many minutes until the next bus showed up at his local stop, he had to hack the firmware and establish a communication link to a Raspberry Pi to do the heavy lifting. The first step was to get a modified firmware on the clock PCB, and that required a ST-LINK V2 programmer and some time tracing out the pins on the STM8 microcontroller to determine how they controlled the various elements of the Nixie tubes. Fortunately, there were just I/O pins left over to stand up a serial link to a Raspberry Pi Zero through a level converter. events.excerpt: TL;DR: Chainlink and Moody's Ratings completed a cross-chain distribution pilot using test data. It ran on testnets and did not publish live rating actions or change Moody's existing publication processes. Tokenized finance needs information to move alongside assets. In a November 10 announcement , Chainlink and Moody's Ratings reported a completed pilot that used the Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol, or CCIP, to distribute credit information across multiple networks. The exercise connected Moody's Token Integration Engine, known as TIE, with cross-chain messaging. Its significance lies in a familiar market problem: investors need consistent information about an instrument even when different pieces of financial infrastructure represent or hold it. A ratings-distribution test with defined limits The pilot used representative data in a controlled testnet environment, spanning permissioned and permissionless networks. No actual rating actions were published onchain, and live dissemination processes were not involved. That scope makes the result useful as an interoperability test. It leaves the separate work of operating a production service, setting responsibilities and integrating it with financial institutions. Consider a hypothetical bond represented across several networks
events.headline: Chainlink and Moody’s Complete Testnet Pilot for Cross-Chain Credit Ratings
